newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-NORWAY PROTESTS OVER CROWDED WORLD CUP CALENDAR.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-NORWAY PROTESTS OVER CROWDED WORLD CUP CALENDAR.

text.p: Norway's Alpine ski team have made an official protest, saying the crowded race calendar is killing the original aims of the Worl d Cup.

"During this year's World Cup in Val d'Isere, the Norwegian Alpine ski team experienced again what will slowly kill the Alpine World Cup in its original form," the team said in a statement released on Thursday.
Because of bad weather in the French resort last weekend a men's downhill was delayed from Saturday to Sunday and a super-giant slalom moved to Monday from Sunday.
Norway, which won the overall World Cup last season with Lasse Kjus, said the changes meant racers who were all-rounders and competed in all disciplines were penalised.
Kjus returned to Norway from France on Monday suffering from a severe sore throat and will be out of action for at least a week.
"We cannot accept a programme that ends up with six races in eight days," the team statement said. "This kills the racers and gives no space for improvement of the sport itself."

It said that the Val d'Isere changes meant Norwegian skiers had to race a super-G at 1200 on Monday December 16 and then drive for eight hours to be ready for a slalom the next day in the Italian resort of Madonna di Campiglio.
They then had to set off immediately after the race to be in Val Gardena for downhill training the following day.
"This shows that there is absolutely no chance for training in between and the performances being made by the racers will be of less quality," the Norwegian statement said.
It added that the week's programme would also make the racers more vulnerable to "a higher risk of injury."
Kjetil-Andre Aamodt, the other Norwegian all-rounder, fell during Thursday's final downhill training here.
"He was so tired yesterday," said Norwegian team press manager Lars Otto Bjoernland, while not linking Kjus's illness or Aamodt's fall directly to the calendar.
There was no immediate reaction from International Ski Federation (FIS) officials in Val Gardena.
Bjoernland said the FIS needed to show they were committed to the importance of the overall World Cup.

He suggested that five races in each discipline could be designated in advance as counting towards the overall World Cup title, thereby allowing the all-rounders to miss those competitions that did not carry the vital points.
Val Gardena is scheduled to host two downhills on Friday and Saturday, before racers move to Alta Badia for a giant slalom on Sunday, the last race before Christmas.
